findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler was changed from a concrete DetectorHandler (which implemented `evaluate` returning `[]`) to `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[...]): pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler is an abc.ABC that declares `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` as abstract, so this class implements none of them and remains abstract. Any code that resolves a Detector of type `metric_alert_fire` will call `Detector.detector_handler`, which does `group_type.detector_handler(self)` and therefore raises `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...`. Previously this path returned an empty result set without error and without throwing, so this is a behavioral regression that will surface as an unhandled exception during detector processing rather than a graceful no-op. Either provide real implementations, or make the property/class fail explicitly with a clear NotImplementedError / skip before instantiation.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` docstring still reads 'Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`', but the method's return type and implementation were changed in this PR to return a `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]` keyed by group key. Callers reading the docstring will be misled about the shape of the return value (e.g. iterating over it yields keys, not results). Update the docstring to describe the dict return value.
